text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nimble Holdings Ltd, whose principal subsidiary is the National Merchant Bank of Zimbabwe (NMB), is coming onto the stock market with a Z$54 million flotation in March, sources told the Zimbabwe Independent. But NMB chief executive Julius Makoni denied that the company a listing although he admitted that last year it indicated it would go public within 18 months.

- The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe will soon be phasing out the current 10 and 20 dollar notes as part of a rationalisation exercise to bring their sizes and designs in line with the new series 50 and 100 notes.

- Zimbabwe's second phase of economic reform, the programme for economic and social transformation, does not have a concrete plan of action through which to achieve its stated objectives, a University of Zimbabwe economics lecturer said recently.
- The Minerals Marketing Corporation of Zimbabwe is battling to recover at least Z$50 million being withheld by an international asbestos marketing agent whose contract was terminated last year.

- The National Railways of Zimbabwe and Siemens International of Germany on Thursday signed an Z$83 million agreement for the rehabiliation of the railways' signalling and control systems on the line between the capital Harare and the eastern city of Mutare.
